test.name: mps-gemm-fp

test.name: image_memory_bandwidth

metric.name: rgba32f
metric.info: Four colour channels at full 32-bit precision: 16 bytes a pixel, the heaviest format here.

metric.name: rgba16f
metric.info: Four channels at half precision: 8 bytes a pixel.

metric.info: Four 8-bit channels: 4 bytes a pixel, the format ordinary images use.

metric.info: A single 32-bit channel: also 4 bytes a pixel, but one value instead of four.

test.name: texture_sample_rate
test.description: How many filtered texture lookups per second the GPU's sampling hardware performs. Every lookup falls between pixels, so the hardware must blend four of them -- the basic operation of drawing any textured surface. The texture is small enough to stay cached, so this measures the sampling units rather than memory.

metric.name: rgba8
metric.info: Blending four 8-bit-per-channel pixels, the common case in games and UI.

metric.name: rgba16f
metric.info: Blending four half-precision pixels -- twice the data per lookup, so the rate typically drops.

test.name: kernel_launch_latency
test.description: The overhead of asking the GPU to do anything at all, measured with a kernel that does no work. It is what small, frequent GPU jobs pay before any of their own work begins.

metric.name: dispatch
metric.info: One way only: from the moment the CPU submits the work to the moment the GPU starts running it.

metric.name: roundtrip
metric.info: The full round trip -- submit, run, and hear back that it finished. This is what the CPU waits for if it has nothing else to get on with.

test.description: Peak speed of the CPU's built-in matrix engine -- Intel AMX tiles or Arm SMMLA/SME -- on 8-bit whole numbers, the format quantized neural networks use.

metric.name: matrix_int8 ST

test.name: aes_encrypt_neon_aes
test.description: How many bytes per second the CPU's dedicated AES instructions encrypt -- the ceiling for disk encryption and HTTPS traffic.

metric.name: aes ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: aes MT
metric.info: Every hardware thread at once -- the whole chip.

test.name: sha256_hash_neon_sha2
test.description: How many bytes per second the CPU hashes with SHA-256, the fingerprint function behind signatures, integrity checks and git-style content addressing.

metric.name: sha256 ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: sha256 MT

test.name: sha512_hash_neon_sha512
test.description: How many bytes per second the CPU hashes with SHA-512, the wider member of the same family. Only Arm cores have an instruction for it today.

metric.name: sha512 ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: sha512 MT
metric.info: Every hardware thread at once -- the whole chip.

test.name: crc32c_armv8_crc32
test.description: How many bytes per second the CPU checksums with CRC32-C, the corruption check storage and network stacks run over every block and packet.

metric.name: crc32c ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: crc32c MT
metric.info: Every hardware thread at once -- the whole chip.

test.name: string_scan_neon
test.description: How fast the CPU hunts through memory for one particular byte -- what memchr, strlen and every text search do. The data fits in L1 cache, so this is the scanning machinery, not memory speed.

metric.name: byte_scan ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: byte_scan MT
metric.info: Every hardware thread at once -- the whole chip.

test.name: utf8_validate_neon
test.description: How fast the CPU checks that text is well-formed UTF-8 -- the first thing every parser, browser and web server does to incoming text. Also run on L1-resident data.

metric.name: utf8 ST
metric.info: One thread, running on a single core.

metric.name: utf8 MT
metric.info: Every hardware thread at once -- the whole chip.

test.name: global_memory_bandwidth
test.description: How many bytes per second all cores together can move to and from main memory. The arrays are far too big for any cache, so every access goes out to RAM.

metric.name: read
metric.info: Reading one large array straight through, start to end.

metric.name: copy
metric.info: Copying one large array into another -- a read and a write for every element.

metric.name: triad
metric.info: Scaling one array, adding a second and storing to a third: two reads and a write per element, the hardest of the three.

test.name: cache_bandwidth
test.description: How many bytes per second the CPU can read out of each cache, from the tiny fast one next to the core to the big slow one shared by all of them. Each reading uses a working set sized to stay inside the cache it names.

metric.name: L1 ST
metric.info: One thread reading from the small cache inside its own core.

metric.name: L1 MT
metric.info: Every core reading from its own L1 at the same time.

metric.name: L2 ST
metric.info: One thread reading from the mid-level cache, the next step out.

metric.name: L2 MT
metric.info: Every core reading from L2 at once; where L2 is shared, the data is split between them so it still fits.

metric.name: L3 ST
metric.info: One thread reading from the large cache shared by all cores.

metric.name: L3 MT
metric.info: Every core reading from that shared cache at once, each taking a slice of it.

test.name: l1_write_bandwidth
test.description: How many bytes per second a core can write into its nearest cache, and copy within it. Cores have fewer paths out to memory than in, so writing usually lands below the matching read row.

metric.name: write ST
metric.info: One thread storing new values into its own L1.

metric.name: write MT
metric.info: Every core storing into its own L1 at the same time.

metric.name: copy ST
metric.info: One thread copying inside L1 -- one read plus one write for every byte moved.

metric.name: copy MT
metric.info: Every core copying inside its own L1 at the same time.

test.name: memory_latency
test.description: How long the core waits for one memory read when it has nothing else to do -- each read's address comes from the previous read, so the hardware cannot start the next one early.

metric.name: L1
metric.info: Reading from the small cache inside the core.

metric.name: L2
metric.info: Reading from the mid-level cache, after an L1 miss.

metric.name: L3
metric.info: Reading from the last-level cache shared between cores.

metric.name: DRAM
metric.info: Reading from main memory at random -- the worst case.

metric.name: DRAM linear
metric.info: Main memory again, but read in address order, so the hardware can fetch ahead -- the best case DRAM gets.

metric.name: DRAM x8
metric.info: Eight independent chases at once: the reads overlap instead of waiting in turn, so each costs less.

metric.name: DRAM x32
metric.info: Thirty-two chases at once -- deep enough that the core runs out of room for further overlap, so the cost per read stops falling.

metric.name: TLB miss
metric.info: The address-translation cost on its own: the data is cached, but every read lands on a different page.

test.name: atomics
test.description: How long one all-or-nothing counter update takes. This is the operation behind locks, reference counts and every shared data structure, so it sets the cost of coordinating between threads.

metric.name: uncontended ST
metric.info: One thread updating a counter nobody else touches, so it stays in that core's own cache.

metric.name: contended MT
metric.info: Every core fighting over the same counter, which has to be handed from core to core -- the time between completed updates anywhere on the chip.

test.name: branch_mispredict
test.description: What it costs when the CPU guesses the wrong way at an if-statement. The same loop runs over sorted data (easy to guess) and shuffled data (a coin flip), and the difference is the price of a wrong guess.

metric.name: predicted
metric.info: Time per if-statement on sorted data, where the CPU guesses right every time.

metric.name: random
metric.info: Time per if-statement on shuffled data, where the CPU is wrong about half the time.

metric.name: penalty
metric.info: The extra time one wrong guess costs, worked out from the gap between the other two readings.

test.name: store_forward
test.description: How fast the core can read back a value it just wrote, without the write having reached the cache yet.
